The AI Trust Maturity Model Five steps from saying it to proving it.

Five steps describing how well you can prove a control works, from “somebody says so” to “it stays true on its own”. For each level it shows what is physically in the room, and the one question that settles where you are.

ONE PAGEFIVE LEVELSFREE TO USE AND ADAPT
The model

Pick a level to see what it looks like from the inside.

You believe the control is there because somebody says it is.

What exists here

A policy, a slide, or a supplier assurance. Nothing that can be examined.

How to tell

Ask who last looked. If the answer is a name and no date, you are here.

The move up

Write down what exists. An honest inventory is the whole of level two.

The gap between two levels is almost always one artifact.

Between asserted and documented it is an inventory. Between documented and evidenced it is a decision record. Between evidenced and tested it is a tester who does not own the control. Each one is cheap to keep as you go, and expensive to reconstruct after the fact.

How to use it

Two ways to use it, and one to avoid.

01

As a shared vocabulary

It gives a board and an engineering team the same word for the same thing, which removes most of the argument.

02

As a starting point

Score yourself before you buy anything. If you land on level four, what you need is a cadence that keeps you there, not a new project.

03

Not as a score to chase

Level five on a system nobody uses is worth less than level three on the one carrying your revenue. Scope first.

Score yourself in three minutes.

Ten statements, answered honestly. Nothing is submitted and nothing is stored.
